extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Dietary information was collected by an in-person interview with a detailed quantitative dietary history.

studies.Title: Flavonoid intake and risk of chronic diseases.
studies.Reference: Flavonoid intake and risk of chronic diseases.
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Timing: dietary intake in the year preceding baseline with subsequent register-based incident case identification
studies.Population: 10 054 men and women; prostate cancer analysis in men
studies.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of myricetin intake

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The total dietary intakes of 10 054 men and women during the year preceding the baseline examination were determined with a dietary history method.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Men with higher quercetin intakes had a lower lung cancer incidence (0.42; 0.25, 0.72; P = 0.001), and men with higher myricetin intakes had a lower prostate cancer risk (0.43; 0.22, 0.86; P = 0.002).
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The relative risk (RR) between the highest and lowest quartiles was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.63, 0.99: P for trend = 0.02). The incidence of cerebrovascular disease was lower at higher kaempferol (0.70; 0.56, 0.86; P = 0.003), naringenin (0.79; 0.64, 0.98; P = 0.06), and hesperetin (0.80; 0.64, 0.99; P = 0.008) intakes.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: men with higher myricetin intakes had a lower prostate cancer risk (0.43; 0.22, 0.86; P = 0.002)
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: The relative risk (RR) between the highest and lowest quartiles was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.63, 0.99: P for trend = 0.02).
extraction_supporting_text.design: The incident cases of the diseases considered were identified from different national public health registers.
extraction_supporting_text.timing: during the year preceding the baseline examination
extraction_supporting_text.continent: mainly on the basis of the flavonoid concentrations in Finnish foods
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Flavonoid intakes were estimated, mainly on the basis of the flavonoid concentrations in Finnish foods.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 1.06 (95% CI: 0.81–1.38), indicating no statistically significant association between antioxidants and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 86.10%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
